A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Palimpsa study. Their complete main texts, appendices, equations, tables, and figures are readable and support reliable matching across relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original MQAR experiments, language-model evaluations, metaplasticity ablations, learning-dynamics analyses, and inference-throughput measurements.

after.justification: v3 retains these empirical results and adds original 2.7B-model evaluations, LongBench and RULER results, and memory diagnostics.

M1.justification: The Palimpsa recurrence and existing variants remain unchanged. Section 3.4 and Appendix A.10 introduce a targeted hybrid conversion: replace the eight Mamba2 layers with the largest median memory windows while retaining the other 56 layers. v1 only suggested future selective use of metaplasticity.

E1.justification: v3 adds LongBench and RULER evaluation, covering long-context retrieval, tracing, aggregation, and question answering. Appendix A.10 also adds training on StackV2 code, SlimPajamas arxiv/book subsets, synthetic Needle-in-a-Haystack data, and LongAlpaca. This substantially extends the retained MQAR, FineWeb-Edu, and standard language-task coverage.

E2.justification: Corresponding experiments retain Gated Deltanet, Transformer++, non-metaplastic Palimpsa variants, and Simple GLA for throughput. The new 2.7B comparisons use the same Mamba2-equivalent Palimpsa-M without metaplasticity comparator. No distinct comparison method is introduced or removed.

E3.justification: v3 adds a 2.7B checkpoint pretrained on 300B tokens, followed by matched baseline/hybrid training with 10B continued-pretraining tokens, 5B context-extension tokens, and instruction tuning. It adds per-position NLL evaluation and RULER testing from 4k to 32k. The stated throughput configuration also changes from B=1, L=32 to B=16, L=2048; the unchanged plot does not establish that measurements were rerun.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained ablations and MQAR learning dynamics, v3 adds per-token WikiText NLL analysis of memory degradation (Figure 4), layer-wise memory-window diagnostics supporting selective replacement (Figure 6), and context-length sensitivity analysis on RULER. These substantially expand investigation of when and where metaplasticity helps.

E5.justification: The eight-seed MQAR reporting and standard-deviation displays are unchanged, and the new large-model results provide no additional run counts or significance tests. New Figure 4 contains shaded bands whose meaning and construction are undefined, preventing a reliable judgment about whether uncertainty-reporting procedures have expanded.

E6.justification: New results include 2.7B average accuracy of 59.22 versus 60.06 and LongBench overall scores of 19.3 versus 20.4 for baseline versus Palimpsa. RULER results are mixed: variable tracing scores are 59.6 versus 33.5 at 4k, but 14.9 versus 24.4 at 32k. The retained Table 2 changes the 170M fine-tuned Palimpsa-M average from 43.41 to 43.48; existing plots remain unchanged.

T1.justification: v3 corrects Equation 1's predictive normalization, missing factors in the free-energy expression, and the Mesa matrix-multiplication order in Table 1 and Appendix A.4. Appendix A.3 adds an explicit Sherman-Morrison update and discusses its limitation under forgetting. These are localized mathematical corrections and extensions; the Palimpsa update remains unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract and four principal contributions remain unchanged. The introduction and conclusion extend the empirical claim to long-context benchmarks and specifically claim successful memory extension through replacement of only eight layers in a pretrained 2.7B model. This modestly extends the practical scope of the existing conversion claim.

C2.justification: v3 adds an explanation for weaker from-scratch Palimpsa-D training and substantive applicability boundaries from RULER: shorter-context tracing losses, aggregation weaknesses, and mixed question answering. Appendix A.11 proposes different mechanisms for single-item and multiple-item retrieval. Its claim of consistent N-MK wins is overstated, however: Table 6 reports 21.8 versus the baseline's 24.6 at 8k.

D1.justification: v3 adds a code-repository pointer and documents the 2.7B base checkpoint, 64-layer architecture, width, vocabulary size, layer-selection procedure, training datasets, and three training stages. These substantially expand reproducibility information. Existing small-model hyperparameters and kernel details remain; the bscale initialization range added to Section 2.4 was already documented in v1's appendix.

R1.justification: v3 adds references for LongBench v2, RULER, and long-context training, and revises the Mesa derivation's attribution. Separate hypernetwork and FLA-library references disappear. The substantive positioning relative to Bayesian ICL, continual learning, Longhorn, and Mesanet remains largely unchanged; numerous other reference edits are publication-metadata updates.

P1.justification: Most existing prose remains intact. v3 makes local paragraph and terminology edits, reorders the conclusion, adds Section 3.4, numbers previously unnumbered appendix sections, and corrects cross-references. It also replaces the template running header with the paper title.

P2.justification: v3 adds the NLL plot and layer-wise memory-window visualization, introduces LongBench/RULER tables, and expands Table 2 with a 2.7B block. Existing figures are retained but several are relocated or renumbered. The added plots and structured result displays substantially expand the visual presentation.

improvement.justification: v1 supported long-context memory claims mainly through MQAR and standard language scores. v3 directly tests those claims with matched-training 2.7B comparisons, LongBench/RULER evaluations, and memory diagnostics, while exposing important task-dependent failures. Mathematical corrections and added reproducibility information further strengthen the paper. Undefined NLL bands and overstated retrieval-consistency prose limit interpretation, but the new direct validation substantially improves the evidence for the central claims.
